experiment_kind: paper methods restored on pinned modern author code

mpc.control_parameterization: one historical cubic segment, four knots per force, 48 total parameters

failure.description: Native gym_quadruped invalid non-leg/foot ground contact; no added roll/pitch or height cutoff

video.selection: all fig4; seed 0 and lowest-index failed and successful table1 episodes for each method, without cutting

implementation_choices: Paper omits numerical Q/R/covariance and episode duration. Restore sampling Q, sigma and one-segment cubic interpolation from historical author commit 5c763068; keep acados Q/R from the same source (unchanged in pinned version). Their internal Q differs; compare common physical task metrics, not optimizer cost.

Paper says 21 kg; both pinned modern and historical author configuration say approximately 24.638 kg. Keep actual MJCF and measure total mass/inertia from initial pose for both controllers; do not rescale only the optimizer.

Historical and modern author naive sampler use two Gaussians plus a uniform component at fixed scales. Preserve this actual author implementation despite V-A's shorthand 'multiple Gaussian distributions'; previous mean is retained as one candidate.

Enable the paper's input-force cost in sampling, with the pinned nominal acados 0.001 force weights; paper gives no R values and both historical/modern sampling code comment out this term. Mask nominal stance load on swing legs. Common reported quadratic metric uses nominal acados Q/R, independently of sampling optimizer Q.
Disable foothold optimization, integrators, external wrench compensation, reflexes, velocity modulation, gradient refinement, Riccati feedback, and OT-MPC.

Restore historical scipy cubic swing, gains 5000/100, step height 0.3*hip_height. Preserve author's foothold velocity average and 5 cm velocity-error correction clipping (implementation detail omitted from Eq.3).
Correct adaptive prediction contact phase to begin at current phase, as non-adaptive execution does. Frequency updates at swing apex follow historical author implementation.
Figure 4: explicit world-y command 0.1 m/s; world-y 40 N from 2 to 5 s. Native environment contact termination only; no invented early abort for orientation/height.

Table I omits episode duration, command, wrench schedule and failure threshold. Use 60 s author simulation default, Fig.3 command and 2 s wrench holds, and native gym_quadruped invalid-contact termination. Exact numerical reproduction cannot be claimed.
Reported paper success 37 percent is incompatible with 50 integer Bernoulli episodes. Preserve integer outcomes; do not force match.
Paper Mean Cost/tracking error scalar is not fully defined. Report linear-velocity error norm (m/s), RMSE, integrated quadratic state/input cost and success counts separately.
JIT compilation first solve is retained in raw data and separated from steady-state solve-time boxplot; no dummy warm-up runs.

The initial modern-weight r1-v1 Fig.3 run failed at 5.308 s (naive) and 1.484 s (MPPI). This source-restoration revision replaces modern weights/scales/splines with the fixed historical author's values, not a fitted parameter search. All earlier outcomes remain under r1-v1.

r1-v2 included author-Q restoration, but still used modern swing gains and custom early orientation/height termination. r1-v3 restores historical low-level settings and uses native contact termination. Completed and interrupted r1-v2 data retained; not pooled with final results.

Remove post-paper horizontal-force scaling introduced by 6e7eb08 on 2025-04-14; historical force parameters directly represent N in all three axes. r1-v3 sampling batches interrupted when this omitted restoration was found; all completed episodes retained, then full affected batches rerun as r1-v4.

Acados data from r1-v3 have identical robot, task, low-level and optimizer conditions; only the sampling implementation changed in r1-v4. Reuse those original trajectories with explicit origin in the final comparison.
